p.src: While they were speaking, several young maids and old serving-women hurried up, all laughing. “A great many young ladies and mistresses have arrived, and we do not know any of them! Mistresses and young ladies, do hurry over and claim your relatives.” Li Wan laughed. “What sort of talk is that? Tell us plainly whose relatives they are.” The old women and maids all laughed. “Your two younger sisters have both arrived, Mistress. There is also a young lady said to be Miss Xue’s younger sister, and a young gentleman said to be Master Xue’s younger brother. We are going to fetch Her Ladyship your aunt now, so the mistresses and young ladies should go on ahead.” With that, they went straight on their way. Baochai laughed. “Can it be that our Xue Ke and his sister have come?” Li Wan laughed too. “Can it be that our aunt has come up to the capital again? But they could hardly have arrived together. This is strange indeed.” Thoroughly puzzled, they went to Lady Wang’s principal apartments and found the place densely crowded with people.

p.src: It turned out that Lady Xing’s elder brother and his wife had brought their daughter Xiuyan to the capital to seek Lady Xing’s help. As it happened, Wang Xifeng’s elder brother Wang Ren was also bound for the capital, so the two related families had joined forces for the journey. When they moored their boat midway, they chanced to meet Li Wan’s widowed aunt, who was likewise travelling to the capital with her two daughters—the elder named Li Wen and the younger Li Qi. Once they had compared their connections, they discovered that they too were relatives, and so the three families travelled on together. Behind them came Xue Pan’s cousin Xue Ke. Years before, when their father had been in the capital, he had betrothed Xue Ke’s own younger sister, Xue Baoqin, to the son of Academician Mei. Xue Ke was now taking her to the capital for her marriage, and, hearing that Wang Ren was travelling there, had brought his sister after the others. Thus they had all come together that day to visit and seek out their respective relatives. After everyone had exchanged greetings and recounted their news, Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang were both delighted beyond measure. Grandmother Jia laughed and said, “No wonder the lampwick blossomed and crackled again and again last night, knotting flower after flower. It was all an omen of today.” While chatting about family matters, they inspected the gifts the visitors had brought and ordered wine and a meal to be served so that they might stay and dine. Needless to say, Xifeng became busier than ever. Li Wan and Baochai naturally exchanged all the feelings of their long separation with their aunts and sisters. Daiyu was happy at first to see them, but then she reflected that everyone had relatives while she alone was solitary, without a single kinsman. Inevitably, she went away and shed tears once more. Baoyu understood her feelings well and comforted her at length before the matter was settled.

p.src: Afterwards, Baoyu hurried back to Happy Red Court and said laughingly to Xiren, Sheyue, Qingwen, and the others, “Why don’t you hurry over and see them? Who would have thought that, although Cousin Bao’s own elder brother is the way he is, this cousin of hers should be altogether different in appearance and bearing—he looks more like her own true brother. More remarkable still, you are always saying that Cousin Bao is a peerless beauty, but now you must look at her younger sister, and at Sister-in-law Li’s two younger sisters as well. I simply cannot find words to describe them. Heavens, heavens! What boundless purity and spiritual grace you possess, to bring such surpassing people into being! Now I know what a frog in a well I have been, forever declaring the few people around us to be unique in all the world. Yet there was no need to seek far afield: here are beauties close at hand, each surpassing the last. Today I have gained yet another measure of wisdom. Can there possibly be still more besides these?” As he spoke, he laughed and sighed to himself. Seeing him fall into another of his rapturous fits, Xiren refused to go and look. Qingwen and the others had already been to see the newcomers. When they returned, they giggled and said to Xiren, “Do hurry over and look! The First Lady’s niece, Miss Bao’s younger sister, and Mistress Li’s two younger sisters—they are just like four fresh green scallion stems gathered in a single handful.”

p.src: Before she had finished speaking, Tanchun came in smiling to look for Baoyu and said, “Our poetry club is flourishing now.” Baoyu laughed. “Indeed it is. You were inspired to found the club, and by some uncanny providence all these people have now arrived. There is only one question: have they ever learned to compose poetry?” Tanchun said, “I asked them all just now. Though they spoke modestly, from what I could see, every one of them knows how. Even if one did not, that would be no great difficulty. Just look at Xiangling.” Xiren laughed. “They say Miss Xue’s younger sister is even finer. What does Third Miss think of her?” “It is quite true,” said Tanchun. “In my opinion, neither her elder sister nor any of the others can compare with her.” Xiren was astonished and laughed. “How extraordinary! How could anyone be better than they are? I must go and see her for myself.” Tanchun said, “The moment Grandmother saw her, she was beside herself with delight and has already pressed Mother into accepting her as an adopted daughter. Grandmother wants to keep her here, and it was settled only moments ago.” Overjoyed, Baoyu hastily asked, “Is that really true?” Tanchun replied, “When have I ever lied?” Then she laughed. “Now that she has such a lovely granddaughter, she has forgotten her grandson.” Baoyu laughed. “I do not mind that. It is only right that girls should be cherished more. Tomorrow is the sixteenth; we ought to convene the club.” Tanchun said, “Miss Lin has only just recovered, and Second Sister has fallen ill again. Everything is still unsettled.” Baoyu said, “Second Sister seldom writes poetry anyway. What harm is there if she is absent?” Tanchun said, “We might as well wait a few days. Once the newcomers have become acquainted with us, would it not be pleasant to invite them too? At present, Sister-in-law and Cousin Bao naturally have no heart for poetry; moreover, Xiangyun has not arrived, Daiyu has only just recovered, and no one is quite ready. Better to wait until Xiangyun comes, the newcomers have settled in, Daiyu is fully recovered, Sister-in-law and Cousin Bao have peace of mind, and Xiangling’s poetry has improved. Then we can gather a full company—would that not be better? For now, let us both go to Grandmother and hear what has been decided. Cousin Bao’s younger sister need not be counted, for she is certainly staying with our family. If the other three are not to stay with us, we shall beg Grandmother to keep them in the Garden. Then our company will gain several more members and become all the merrier.” Baoyu’s face lit up with delight when he heard this, and he hastily said, “You are the sensible one. I am muddle-headed after all: I merely rejoiced for a while and never thought of any of that.”

p.src: With that, brother and sister went together to Grandmother Jia’s quarters. Sure enough, Lady Wang had already accepted Baoqin as her adopted daughter. Grandmother Jia was so delighted that she would not even let Baoqin live in the Garden, but had her sleep with her at night. Xue Ke took up residence in Xue Pan’s study. Grandmother Jia said to Lady Xing, “Your niece need not go home either. Let her stay in the Garden for a few days and enjoy herself before she leaves.” Lady Xing’s brother and sister-in-law were poor, and in coming to the capital they had depended upon Lady Xing to find them lodging and help with their travel expenses. Naturally, they were only too willing to accept this proposal. Lady Xing therefore entrusted Xiuyan to Xifeng. Xifeng reflected that the Garden already housed many young ladies of differing temperaments, while it would be inconvenient to establish a separate household for Xiuyan. The best course was to send her to live with Yingchun; then, if Xiuyan should later suffer any dissatisfaction, even if Lady Xing heard of it, Xifeng herself could not be blamed. Thereafter, apart from any days Xiuyan spent at home, whenever she stayed in Prospect Garden for a full month, Xifeng gave her an allowance equal to Yingchun’s. Observing Xiuyan dispassionately, Xifeng judged that her nature and conduct were quite unlike those of Lady Xing and her parents: she was in fact gentle, warmhearted, and lovable. Because Xifeng also pitied her poverty and hard lot, she showed Xiuyan more affection than the other girls, while Lady Xing scarcely concerned herself with the matter.

p.src: Grandmother Jia and Lady Wang had always admired Li Wan’s virtue and kindness, and respected her for remaining chaste in widowhood while still young. Now that her widowed aunt had arrived, they would not allow her to lodge outside the mansion. Although Aunt Li repeatedly declined, Grandmother Jia insisted and would not hear otherwise, so she had no choice but to settle in Paddy-Sweet Cottage with Li Wen and Li Qi.

p.src: Once all these arrangements had been made, it happened that Shi Nai, Marquis of Baoling, was appointed to a high provincial post and would soon depart with his family to assume office. Grandmother Jia could not bear to part with Xiangyun, so she kept her behind and brought her into the household, intending at first to have Xifeng prepare separate quarters for her. But Shi Xiangyun firmly refused and insisted upon living with Baochai, so the plan was abandoned.

p.src: By this time Prospect Garden had become livelier than ever. Li Wan headed the company; then came Yingchun, Tanchun, Xichun, Baochai, Daiyu, Xiangyun, Li Wen, Li Qi, Baoqin, and Xing Xiuyan; with Xifeng and Baoyu added, they numbered thirteen in all. In age, Li Wan was the eldest; the other twelve were all no more than fifteen, sixteen, or seventeen. Three might share one year of birth and five another; two might have been born on the same day of the same month, and two others at the very same hour. Most differed only in their month or time of birth. Even they themselves could not distinguish their seniority precisely and simply called one another “younger brother,” “elder brother,” “elder sister,” or “younger sister” as the whim took them.

p.src: Xiangling now had her whole heart set on writing poetry, yet she dared not pester Baochai too much. As luck would have it, Shi Xiangyun arrived. Shi Xiangyun was exceedingly fond of talking, and when Xiangling began asking her about poetry, she could hardly contain herself; her enthusiasm mounted, and she held forth day and night without pause. Baochai laughed. “I truly cannot endure this endless chatter any longer. For young ladies to go on discussing poetry as though it were serious business—if learned people heard you, they would laugh at you for forgetting your proper place. One muddle-headed Xiangling was trouble enough, and now you have joined her, such an inexhaustible bag of words! Your mouths are full of Du Gongbu’s profound restraint, Wei Suzhou’s淡雅 elegance, Wen Bacha’s ornate luxuriance, and Li Yishan’s obscure subtlety. You fail to recognize two living poets right before you, yet why keep bringing up those dead men?” Hearing this, Xiangyun hastily asked with a laugh, “Which two? Dear sister, do tell me.” Baochai replied with a smile, “Foolish Xiangling, whose heart labors sorely; madcap Xiangyun, whose tongue runs freely.” Xiangyun and Xiangling both burst out laughing.

p.src: As they were speaking, Baoqin came in wearing a cape that glittered with gold and emerald hues, though no one could tell what it was made of. Baochai promptly asked, “Where did that come from?” Baoqin laughed. “Because sleet began to fall, Grandmother found this for me.” Xiangling stepped forward to examine it. “No wonder it is so beautiful—it is woven from peacock feathers.” “Those are not peacock feathers,” said Xiangyun. “It is made from the feathers on wild ducks’ heads. That shows how fond Grandmother is of you. Fond as she is of Baoyu, she has never given it to him to wear.” Baochai said, “As the proverb truly says, ‘Each person has a destiny of their own.’ She could never have expected to arrive just now, and once here, to be so doted upon by Grandmother.” Xiangyun said, “Apart from attending Grandmother, stay here in the Garden; in those two places you may play, laugh, eat, and drink as you please. When you go to Madam’s rooms, if she is there, you may chat and laugh with her and stay awhile; but if she is absent, do not go in. The people there are wicked at heart and are all plotting to harm us.” Her words made Baochai, Baoqin, Xiangling, Ying’er, and the others laugh. Baochai said with a laugh, “One calls you thoughtless, yet you can be thoughtful; but even when you are thoughtful, your tongue is still far too blunt. Our Qin’er here is rather like you. You are forever asking me to be your own sister, so today I shall have you recognize her as your own younger sister instead.” Xiangyun studied Baoqin for quite some time, then laughed. “Only she is worthy of wearing this garment. It truly would not suit anyone else.” While they were still speaking, Hupo came in and said with a smile, “Grandmother says Miss Bao is not to keep too tight a rein on Miss Qin. She is still young, so let her do whatever she likes. Whatever she wants, she should simply ask for it and not worry about imposing.” Baochai promptly rose and acknowledged the message, then gave Baoqin a playful shove and laughed. “Who knows where you found such extraordinary good fortune! You had better go, lest we make you feel mistreated. I simply refuse to believe there is anything in which I am inferior to you.” As they spoke, Baoyu and Daiyu both came in, while Baochai continued her teasing. Xiangyun laughed. “Sister Bao, you may be joking, but someone here genuinely feels that way.” Hupo laughed. “There is no one else who is truly vexed—it can only be him.” As she spoke, she pointed at Baoyu. Baochai and Xiangyun both laughed. “He is not that sort of person.” Hupo laughed again. “If it is not him, then it must be her.” With that, she pointed at Daiyu. Xiangyun fell silent. Baochai hastily laughed. “Still less could it be her. My younger sister is just the same as her own sister. She is even fonder of her and cherishes her more than I do, so how could she be vexed? You are talking wild nonsense. What grounds are there for anything she says?”

My younger sister is just the same as her own sister.
She is even fonder of her and cherishes her more than I do, so how could she be vexed?
You are talking wild nonsense.
What grounds are there for anything she says?”

p.src: Baoyu had long known that Daiyu could be somewhat touchy, and he still knew nothing of the recent change between her and Baochai. He had been afraid that Grandmother’s fondness for Baoqin would make Daiyu unhappy; but now, after hearing Xiangyun speak so and Baochai reply in this way, and after studying Daiyu’s voice and expression and finding them unlike those of former days and entirely consistent with Baochai’s words, he was left perplexed and uneasy. He thought, “Those two were never so close before, yet now they seem ten times more intimate than anyone else.” Before long, Lin Daiyu too began calling Baoqin “little sister” at every turn, never once using her name, just as though they were sisters by birth. Baoqin was young and warmhearted, as well as naturally intelligent. She had read books and learned her characters from childhood, and after two days in the Jia household she had already gained a general understanding of its people. She saw, moreover, that none of the young ladies were frivolous, powder-and-paint creatures, and that all were on harmonious terms with her elder sister; she therefore treated none of them with indifference. Among them, she found Lin Daiyu exceptionally distinguished, and so showed Daiyu a quite extraordinary intimacy and respect. Watching them, Baoyu could only marvel silently to himself.

p.src: After Baochai and her sister had gone to Aunt Xue's rooms, Xiangyun went to see Grandmother Jia, while Lin Daiyu returned to her room to rest. Baoyu sought Daiyu out and said with a smile, “Though I have read The Romance of the Western Chamber, there were only a few lines I understood; once, when I quoted them as a joke, you became angry with me. But now that I think of it, there is one line I truly do not understand. I will recite it, and you can explain it to me.” Daiyu knew at once that there was more behind his words and replied with a smile, “Recite it, then. Let me hear.” Baoyu smiled. “There is a marvelous line in ‘The Uproar over the Letter’: ‘When did Meng Guang take up Liang Hong's tray?’ That line is exquisite. ‘Meng Guang took up Liang Hong's tray’ is merely a familiar allusion; what is remarkable is the wit with which the three little words ‘when did’ turn it into a question. When did she take it up? Tell me, so that I may understand.” Hearing this, Daiyu could not help laughing too. “It is indeed a fine question,” she said. The playwright asked it well, and you ask it well too.” Baoyu said, “Before, you alone suspected me; now even you have nothing to say, and I am the one left out in the cold.” Daiyu smiled. “Who would have thought that she truly was a good person? I had always imagined she was concealing treachery.” Beginning with her mistaken quotation during the drinking game, she told Baoyu in detail about the bird's nest Baochai had sent and everything they had discussed during her illness. Only then did Baoyu understand. He laughed and said, “No wonder! I was wondering ‘when Meng Guang took up Liang Hong's tray.’ So she took up the tray from the moment that ‘a child speaks without reserve’!” Daiyu then began speaking of Baoqin; remembering that she herself had no sisters, she could not keep from weeping again. Baoyu hurried to console her. “You are tormenting yourself again. Just look at yourself—you are even thinner this year than last, yet you still will not take care of your health. However well the day begins, you must find something to grieve over and weep for a while before you can consider the day's business done.” Daiyu wiped away her tears. “Lately my heart is always aching, yet I seem to shed fewer tears than I did last year. The pain in my heart goes on and on, but the tears no longer flow so freely.” Baoyu said, “You have cried so often that you only imagine it so. How could one's tears ever run short?”

p.src: As they were speaking, a young maid from Daiyu's room arrived with her scarlet felt cloak and said, “The Young Mistress has just sent word that, since it has snowed, she wants to discuss inviting everyone to compose poetry tomorrow.” Before she had finished, one of Li Wan's maids came to summon Daiyu. Baoyu invited Daiyu to go with him to Paddy-Sweet Cottage. Daiyu changed into little red fragrant-sheepskin boots with gold-trimmed cloud patterns, put on a bright-red feather-gauze cape lined with white fox fur, fastened about her waist a blue-and-gold, green-shimmering double-looped ruyi sash, and covered her head with a snow hood. Together they made their way through the snow. They found all the young ladies gathered there, nearly all alike in bright-red scarlet-felt or feather-satin cloaks. Li Wan alone wore a blue, front-opening woolen jacket, while Xue Baochai wore a dark violet-blue cape of figured brocade, further adorned with foreign-thread embroidery and coarse silk. Xing Xiuyan, however, still wore her ordinary old clothes and had nothing to protect her from the snow. Presently Shi Xiangyun arrived, wearing a coat Grandmother Jia had given her, made of sable heads and lined with thick black-and-grey squirrel fur, so warm both inside and out that it seemed to radiate heat. On her head was a Zhaojun hood of bright-red scarlet felt, patterned with clouds and lined in goose-yellow cloth flecked with gold, and around her neck she wore a broad sable collar. Daiyu was the first to laugh. “Look, everyone—the Monkey King has arrived! Just like him, she carries her snow cloak too, deliberately dressing herself up as a little Tartar dandy.” Xiangyun laughed. “Just look at what I am wearing underneath!” As she spoke, she took off her outer coat. Underneath she wore a somewhat worn, harmoniously colored, triple-bordered, autumn-incense jacket with gold-threaded, multicolored embroidered dragons, narrow lapels, close-fitting sleeves, an overlapping front, and grey-squirrel fur. Beneath that was a short, pale-red figured-satin tunic lined with fox belly fur. A five-colored palace cord with long tassels, tied in a butterfly bow, clasped her waist tightly, and she too wore little doe-hide boots. The outfit made her slender waist, straight back, and lithe, angular figure more striking than ever. Everyone laughed. “She alone insists on dressing like a boy, yet she actually looks prettier this way than when dressed as a girl.” Xiangyun said, “Quick, let us discuss the poetry gathering! Let me hear who is to be our host.” Li Wan said, “It was my idea. Yesterday's proper occasion has already passed, and the next one is too far away. Since it happens to have snowed, why should we not hold a club meeting, welcome our new arrivals, and compose poetry at the same time? What do you all think?” Baoyu spoke first. “That is an excellent idea. Only it is already late today, and if the sky clears tomorrow, it will spoil the fun.” The others looked outside and said, “It may not clear; and even if it does, what falls during the night will be ample for us to admire.” Li Wan said, “Pleasant though this place is, it cannot compare with Reed-Snow Cottage. I have already sent people to heat its floor stove; we can all gather around the brazier and compose our poems.”

p.src: “The Old Lady probably would not be pleased, and since this is only a little amusement of ours, we need merely let Xifeng know. One tael of silver from each of you will be enough; send it all to me.” Pointing to Xiangling, Baoqin, Li Wen, Li Qi, and Xiuyan, she continued, “These five are exempt. Second Cousin is ill, so she does not count, and Fourth Cousin has taken leave, so neither does she. Send me your four contributions, and with the five or six taels I shall add, there will be more than enough.” Baochai and the others all agreed. They then began discussing a theme and rhyme restrictions, but Li Wan laughed and said, “I already have something in mind. When the time comes tomorrow, you will find out soon enough.” After this, they chatted idly for a while before going to Grandmother Jia’s quarters. Nothing further happened that day. Early the next morning, Baoyu, who had been thinking about the gathering and had scarcely slept all night, scrambled out of bed at daybreak. He raised the bed curtains and looked. Though the doors and windows were still closed, the panes shone with dazzling brilliance. His heart sank, for he supposed the sky had cleared and the sun was already up. He hurriedly rose and lifted the inner window frame to look through the glass. It was not sunlight at all: heavy snow had fallen throughout the night, lying more than a foot deep, while flakes still filled the sky like teased and torn wads of cotton. Baoyu was overjoyed. He quickly called the servants to rise and, after washing, put on only an aubergine-colored foreign-cloth fox-fur jacket, over it a short sea-otter cape with wing-shaped shoulders. He fastened his belt, threw on a jade-needle rush cape, donned a golden-rattan hat, stepped into his sandalwood clogs, and hurried away to Reed-Snow Cottage. Outside the courtyard gate, he looked all around and saw only a single expanse of white, save for distant green pines and emerald bamboo; he himself seemed enclosed within a glass case. When he reached the foot of the hill and had just rounded its base, a cold fragrance suddenly brushed his nostrils. Turning his head, he saw a dozen or so red plum trees in Green Lattice Nunnery before Miaoyu’s gate. Crimson as rouge against the snow, they looked exceptionally vivid and spirited—a most enchanting sight. Baoyu stopped and admired them closely for some time before going on. He saw someone approaching under an umbrella on the Humpback Bridge: it was the servant Li Wan had sent to invite Xifeng.

p.src: When Baoyu reached Reed-Snow Cottage, he found the maids and old women sweeping away the snow to clear a path. Reed-Snow Cottage consisted of several rooms built along a riverbank beside the hill and overlooking the water. It had a thatched roof, earthen walls, hibiscus hedges, and bamboo windows; one could fish simply by opening a window. Reeds screened it on every side, and a winding path threaded through them to the bamboo bridge by Lotus-Fragrance Pavilion. Seeing him arrive in cape and hat, the maids and old women laughed. “We were just saying that all we lacked was a fisherman; now the picture is complete. The young ladies will not come until after breakfast. You are far too impatient.” Hearing this, Baoyu had no choice but to turn back. Just as he reached Drenched Blossoms Pavilion, he saw Tanchun coming from Studio of Autumn Freshness. She wore a bright-red felt cloak of orangutan wool and a Guanyin hood, and leaned on a young maid, while behind her a woman held an oiled green-silk umbrella. Knowing that she was going to Grandmother Jia’s quarters, Baoyu waited beside the pavilion until she came up, and the two left the garden together. Baoqin was in the inner room, washing, combing her hair, and changing her clothes.

p.src: Before long all the girls had assembled, while Baoyu kept complaining that he was hungry and repeatedly urged them to serve the meal. At last the dishes were set out, and the first was a milk-steamed suckling lamb. Grandmother Jia said, “This is medicine for old people like us—a creature that never saw the light of day. Unfortunately, it is not suitable for you children. There is fresh venison today as well; wait for that.” They all assented. Baoyu, however, could not wait. He poured tea over a bowl of rice and hastily swallowed it down with minced pheasant and pickled cucumber. Grandmother Jia said, “I knew you had some scheme afoot again today—you cannot even be bothered to eat properly.” She ordered them to “save the venison for him to eat this evening,” but Xifeng quickly assured her that there was more, so she let the matter drop. Shi Xiangyun quietly proposed to Baoyu, “Since there is fresh venison, why don’t we ask for a piece and cook it ourselves in the garden? We can have fun and eat it too.” This was exactly what Baoyu wanted to hear. He promptly asked Xifeng for a piece and told an old woman to carry it into the garden.

Daiyu said, “Those two must never be allowed to get together. Whenever they do, there is no end to the mischief they create. You may eat a whole raw deer for all I care; if you gorge yourselves sick, it will be none of my concern. p.src: Xifeng sent Pinger to say that she could not come, as she was busy distributing the annual allowances. When Xiangyun saw Pinger, she would not hear of letting her go. Pinger too was fond of fun. Having accompanied Xifeng everywhere on ordinary days, she found the occasion so delightful that she gladly joined in the merriment. She slipped the bracelets from her wrists, and the three of them gathered around the brazier, intending first to roast three pieces for themselves. Baochai and Daiyu, who were accustomed to such scenes, thought nothing strange of it, but Baoqin and the others, as well as Aunt Li, found it most extraordinary. Tanchun, Li Wan, and the others had already settled the theme and rhyme. Tanchun laughed. “Just smell it—the aroma reaches all the way over here. I shall go and have some too.” With that, she went over to join them. Li Wan followed her and said, “All the guests are here. Have you still not eaten enough?” Xiangyun said between bites, “It is only when I eat this that I enjoy drinking wine, and only after drinking wine can I compose poetry. Without this venison, I could never compose a poem today.” As she spoke, they saw Baoqin standing there smiling, wrapped in her wild-duck down cloak. Xiangyun laughed. “Silly girl, come over and taste some.” “It looks terribly dirty,” Baoqin said with a laugh. Baochai said, “Go and try it. It is delicious. Your cousin Lin has a weak digestion and could not digest it; otherwise, she would enjoy it too.” At this, Baoqin went over and ate a piece. It was indeed delicious, so she too began eating. Presently Xifeng sent a young maid to summon Pinger. Pinger said, “Miss Shi is keeping hold of me. You go on back first.” The young maid went away. Before long, Xifeng herself appeared in a cloak and said with a laugh, “Eating something so delicious without even telling me!” With that, she joined the group and began eating too. Daiyu laughed. “Where did this band of beggars come from? Enough, enough! Today the Reed-Snow Retreat has suffered a calamity—Yun, that wild girl, has utterly ravaged it. I shall weep a great lament for the Reed-Snow Retreat!” Xiangyun gave a scornful laugh. “What do you know? ‘True scholars are naturally unconventional.’ You are all sham purists, and nothing could be more tiresome. Now we gorge ourselves on rank and gamey meat, but when we return, our hearts will be brocade and our words embroidery.” Baochai laughed. “If your poem turns out poorly later, we shall dig the meat back out of you and stuff in some of these snow-laden reeds instead, thereby bringing this calamity to its proper conclusion.”

Baochai said, “Go and try it. It is delicious.
Your cousin Lin has a weak digestion and could not digest it; otherwise, she would enjoy it too.”
At this, Baoqin went over and ate a piece. It was indeed delicious, so she too began eating.
Presently Xifeng sent a young maid to summon Pinger.
Pinger said, “Miss Shi is keeping hold of me. You go on back first.”
The young maid went away.
Before long, Xifeng herself appeared in a cloak and said with a laugh, “Eating something so delicious without even telling me!”
With that, she joined the group and began eating too.
Daiyu laughed. “Where did this band of beggars come from?
Enough, enough! Today the Reed-Snow Retreat has suffered a calamity—Yun, that wild girl, has utterly ravaged it.
I shall weep a great lament for the Reed-Snow Retreat!”
Xiangyun gave a scornful laugh. “What do you know?
‘True scholars are naturally unconventional.’ You are all sham purists, and nothing could be more tiresome.
Now we gorge ourselves on rank and gamey meat, but when we return, our hearts will be brocade and our words embroidery.”

Baochai laughed. “If your poem turns out poorly later, we shall dig the meat back out of you and stuff in some of these snow-laden reeds instead, thereby bringing this calamity to its proper conclusion.”

Let us hurry and make a few good ones now, ready for our amusement in the first month.”

As they spoke, they all entered the room with the heated brick platform. Cups, dishes, fruit, and vegetables had already been set out, and the prescribed format for the poetic theme and rhymes had been posted on the wall.

Baoyu and Xiangyun hurried to look and saw that the assignment read: “A linked verse on the scene before us: one regulated poem in five-character lines, using rhymes from the second Xiao rhyme group.”
The order of participants had not yet been listed beneath it.
Li Wan said, “I am not very skilled at composing poetry, so I shall contribute only the first three lines. After that, whoever thinks of a line first may add it.”
Baochai said, “We should still decide on an order.”
